1 big thing: Pay-for-play text rocks White House
 
Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photos via Getty Images

Top Trump adviser Ric Grenell allegedly outlined a stunning pay-for-influence offer to a Turkish billionaire last year, Axios' Marc Caputo reports exclusively.

  • The offer to Turkish businessman Turhan Mildon included access to "POTUS," "VIP events" and administration officials, according to a text message that the White House counsel is investigating.

🤳 The May 3, 2025, text to Mildon says: "Once the money comes to the company here, I will arrange the donation to Kennedy Centre [sic], and you'll be joining the VIP events and get close with the administration, even with POTUS."

Administration officials say the text is key evidence in the White House's investigation of whether Grenell misappropriated a potential multimillion-dollar donation to the Kennedy Center, which he led at the time.

  • Mildon is married to another Trump adviser: Alina Habba, former U.S. attorney for New Jersey. She stormed into the Oval Office on Oct. 9 and accused Grenell of hoodwinking her husband into making a Kennedy Center donation that never arrived, Axios first reported.
  • Grenell has called the accusations "lies" and denied sending the text message.

💵 At the heart of the alleged scheme is a financial transaction involving a Houston-based defense company's software and the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mildon and Habba's attorneys have told the White House.

  • Mildon alleges that at Grenell's direction, he wired $17.6 million to Texas Armament & Technology. Mildon says the money was to be split in two parts: one for the Congo deal and nearly $6 million for the Kennedy Center.

Habba told Trump it took 17 months for Mildon to learn the Kennedy Center never received the money he thought was included in the wire sent at Grenell's direction.

  • It's unclear what the Congo contract was for, how it related to the Kennedy Center or what the financial specifics were.

2. 🚁 Evacuation drone takes flight
 
The StarGate drone during a demonstration flight. Photo: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP

A Ukrainian brigade is testing a huge drone designed to carry wounded troops to safety.

  • The aircraft, developed by Ukrainian defense technology company SkyFall, carries a stretcher underneath six sets of propellers.

⛑️ The drone could quickly reach critically injured soldiers deep in areas under threat of Russian attack.

  • AI features and other tech are designed to counter GPS interference now common in Ukraine and other war zones.

💵 The company estimates each system will cost at least $50,000, depending on configuration. It aims to produce up to 1,000 monthly by the end of the year.

4. 🏀 1 sports thing: Gators top preseason poll
 
Data: AP. Chart: Axios

Florida will start the men's college basketball season where the team ended two seasons ago: No. 1.

  • The Gators were the overwhelming pick to top this year's preseason AP Top 25, nabbing 47 of the 59 first-place votes.

🐊 Florida started last season at No. 3, but crashed out of the poll entirely by early January.

  • The Gators rallied to win the Southeastern Conference regular-season championship — only to get stunned by Iowa in the second round of the NCAA Tournament.
